data: First close-up images of a cometary nucleus — 596 km past Halley's Comet, 1986-03-14

ESA's first deep-space probe. Spin-stabilised drum-shaped bus protected by a Whipple-shield dust bumper (Kevlar + aluminum), built around the Halley Multicolour Camera, plus 9 other instruments contributed by 11 European countries + NASA + Japan. Closest approach to 1P/Halley was 1986-03-14T00:03 UTC at 596 km on the sunward side — the bumper survived but a 100 mg dust impact 14 seconds before closest approach offset the spin axis and broke camera contact. Recovered after the encounter, hibernated 1986-1990, then woke for a 200 km flyby of 26P/Grigg-Skjellerup on 1992-07-10 — the first time a spacecraft was reactivated for a second mission target. Final shutdown 1992-07-23.
Reinhard (1986) — The Giotto encounter with comet Halley (Nature 321)
First close-up images of a cometary nucleus — flew 596 km past Halley's Comet at 68 km/s in 1986

ESA's first deep-space probe. Spin-stabilised drum-shaped bus protected by a Whipple-shield dust bumper, built around the Halley Multicolour Camera plus 9 other instruments contributed by 11 European countries, NASA, and Japan. Closest approach to comet 1P/Halley on 1986-03-14 at 596 km — the bumper survived, though a 100 mg dust strike 14 seconds before closest approach offset the spin axis and broke camera contact. Reactivated in 1990 for a 200 km flyby of comet Grigg-Skjellerup in 1992, the first time a spacecraft returned to a different cometary target.
ESA's first deep-space mission; closest comet flyby ever attempted (Halley, 596 km, 1986); first close-up imaging of a cometary nucleus
Europe's first independent orbital launcher — opened the commercial-comsat era for ESA, flew Giotto to Halley
ESA's first Mars orbiter; Europe's first planetary mission
First European Moon mission — solar-electric ion drive. Spiralled to the Moon over 13 months; deliberate impact 2006-09-03
First spacecraft to orbit a comet (67P)
ESA flagship to Jupiter — first orbiter ever to settle around a Galilean moon (Ganymede, 2034)
Soviet Venus + Halley's Comet double mission — Venera lander, first interplanetary balloon, then Halley flyby
